gpt-5.5 and gemini-3.1-pro-preview returned CLEAN. claude-opus-4.8 flagged one substantive non-blocking design flaw prior reviewers missed: Math.max(baseUrgency, chainUrgency) in bt-ai-provider.ts is provably inert. Algebra: chainUrgency non-zero only when onCriticalPath=true; onCriticalPath requires no pre-chain/shop/other segments remain; at that point global segments = chain+staircase+post-stairs identically to chain remainingRequiredMs composition (both = sum(spellBroker)+sum(staircase)+sum(postStairs)+safetyBuffer); identical slack window; identical urgency. Chain work is strict subset of global work so chainUrgency <= globalUrgency unconditionally, with equality when used. Empirical sweep confirmed max delta == 0. Self-verified against run-planner.ts:434-438 and :481. Reported to human sender with 3 options, sender chose A (delete inert block). Applied: removed Math.max block, reverted urgency to runPlan?.urgency ?? panic; removed the one planner test whose author-comment already conceded it could not assert inequality; updated BT test comment to attribute pickup suppression to chainBeeline (real mechanism) not urgency saturation (dead). Retained real mechanisms: chainBeeline detour tightening + chainSuppressionOverride. Post-cleanup: 61/61 targeted tests pass.
rounds.adjudication_notes: Escalated the flaw to the human rather than rationalizing it, per rule #12. Option A keeps the two genuinely new mechanisms and drops the decorative one.
